name: Idealism
summary: Idealism (Ulkuculuk, also Turkesism) is the Turkish-Islamic nationalist creed of Alparslan Turkes and the Nationalist Movement Party, one of the Nine Lights of his doctrine. It puts the Turkish nation and state first, joins Turkish identity to Islamic morals while ranking nationalism above religion when they conflict, and seeks Turkic unity. Its economics is a statist mixed economy with limited property, peasant cooperatives and rapid industrialisation, and it is fiercely anti-communist and opposed to ethnic autonomy.
scope: The Turkish nationalist doctrine of Alparslan Turkes (Nine Lights Doctrine, 1960s onward), as carried by the MHP and the Idealist Hearths and described in its programme and election declarations. Excludes the secular racial Turanism of Nihal Atsiz, the Islamist parties, and the Turkish-Islamic synthesis as adopted by the state, which has its own profile. Economic and social-policy answers are often inferred, so many are low confidence.

sources.title: MHP election declaration 'Toplumsal Onarim ve Huzurlu Gelecek' (Social Repair and Peaceful Future)
sources.author: Nationalist Movement Party (MHP), via Yeni Safak election archive
sources.usedFor: Party positions on unitary state, Turkish-language education, secularism with religious freedom, economy, minimum wage, privatization, unions, women, security.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The declaration mentions free prevention for the disabled and better health access for the elderly and poor but no universal scheme; inferred from its statist social-protection stance.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The programme promises a higher net minimum wage (1,400 TL) and income-tax exemption for minimum-wage earners.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The programme praises private-sector dynamism and competitiveness yet keeps strategic state enterprises, so adherents are split.

public-ownership.rationale: The doctrine endorses a mixed economy with state control of main strategic activities, and the programme keeps strategic assets such as large hydro plants public.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The programme stresses tax fairness and tax relief for production rather than higher rates on the wealthy; no stated position.

unions-good.rationale: The programme extends union rights to more public workers, and the doctrine's societalism favours workers' organization within national unity.

property-fundamental.rationale: Societalism accepts private property but opposes its abuse against the nation, so it is neither absolute nor rejected.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The programme curbs market dominance resulting from privatizations and restructures energy regulation; inferred general tolerance of regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: The programme proposes social protection for the poor and a comprehensive social security system, and societalism backs social assistance.

worker-ownership.rationale: Doctrine offers property within limits and corporatist social harmony, not worker ownership; the programme privatizes via share offerings.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Idealists identify with protecting the state against internal enemies; the programme condemns illegal surveillance though, so the lean is mild.

legalize-drugs.rationale: A conservative moralist nationalist movement stressing morality and Turkish customs would oppose legal recreational drugs; inferred.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The programme wants a free media without censorship but also insists on responsible broadcasting; adherents are split.

strong-leader.rationale: The party-leader-doctrine trilogy and the title Basbug for Turkes show a strong-leader culture.

state-harmful.rationale: Idealists identified the interests of the state with those of the nation and held the state to be necessary to protect homeland and nation.

limit-guns.rationale: The programme emphasises order and state security; inferred support for state monopoly on arms rather than a gun-rights stance.

empower-police-military.rationale: Idealists saw their mission as protecting the state and the programme prioritizes security and domestic defence production.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Morality (the third light) upholds the nation's customs and traditions; inferred opposition.

decide-locally.rationale: The programme aims to preserve the unitary national state, which implies centralized rather than local decision-making.

rehabilitation.rationale: The programme stresses ending terrorism and anarchy and a tough security stance; inferred preference for punishment.

traditional-family.rationale: The programme builds on family protection and the doctrine's morality light stresses the nation's customs and traditions.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Morality grounded in Turkish-Islamic customs and traditions rules this out for a typical adherent.

abortion-legal.rationale: No source discusses abortion; inferred from the Islamic morals and family-centred traditionalism that the morality light and Idealism's Turkish-Islamic character invoke.

more-religion-public.rationale: Idealism ties Turkish identity to Islamic morals and virtues, though nationalism takes precedence and the party is not an Islamic party.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not an issue in the doctrine; its ethno-national Turkish focus makes affirmative remedies for racial groups unlikely.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not discussed by the sources; inferred from a morality light that grounds norms in inherited national customs rather than in constructivist theory.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The nationalism and morality lights centre on preserving the Turkish nation's spirit, customs and traditions.

gradual-change.rationale: Populism wants progress without severing ties to roots, but the movement also promoted rapid industrialization; split.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The programme deters illegal foreign employment and prioritizes the Turkish nation; inferred mild restrictionism.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The programme asserts a Turkey-centered foreign policy and national interest first, not strengthened global bodies.

free-trade.rationale: The programme wants export promotion and diversified trade yet prioritizes domestic agriculture and defence production; mixed.

nation-first.rationale: The declaration's slogan is My country and nation first, and the first light is everything for the Turkish nation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The programme favours a Turkey-centred national-interest foreign policy, while Turkic and Muslim solidarity could justify intervention; no sourced position, so split.

open-borders.rationale: Statism and Turkish ethno-national identity make eventually open borders alien to the doctrine.

limit-growth.rationale: The industrialisation light calls for rapid industrial development; degrowth is contrary.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The programme calls for environmentally sensitive planning and clean energy but prioritizes growth and energy development.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The industrialisation and technology light and the scientific-mentality light are meant to prepare Turkey for the nuclear and space era.

expand-nuclear.rationale: The doctrine anticipates the nuclear and space era; nuclear energy is not directly addressed.

revolution-justified.rationale: Turkes took part in the 1960 coup, but the movement defended the existing state order against revolutionaries; split.

experts-over-public.rationale: The scientific light favours science guiding activities, while populism favours working with the people; no clear stance.

central-planning.rationale: A mixed economy with state control of strategic sectors rejects both socialism and capitalism; full central planning is not endorsed.

socialized-markets.rationale: Worker or public ownership of firms is not part of the doctrine's mixed economy.

land-value-tax.rationale: No source addresses land taxation; the programme speaks only of tax fairness that does not harm production, which does not decide this.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Property is accepted within limits and the family is central; heavy inheritance taxes are not endorsed.

basic-income.rationale: The programme favours work, production and targeted social protection rather than unconditional income.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The programme prioritizes domestic agriculture and domestic defence production over imports.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The doctrine's mixed economy gives the state control of main strategic activities and drives rapid industrialisation.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The peasant-care and societalism lights favour cooperatives, small farmers and spread-out property.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The doctrine is anti-communist and accepts property and a mixed economy.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The programme operates within a state-managed economy; abolishing central banks is alien to it.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The Republican Peasants' Nation Party tradition contained corporatist components, and Fikret Eren proposed mandatory worker unions outside state control.

one-party-rule.rationale: The party competed electorally and joined coalitions; it did not demand a single-party state.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The movement is republican, serving the Turkish state and its Basbug-led nation; monarchy is not part of it.

democracy-best.rationale: The programme and the doctrine nominally include freedom and democracy, though adherents prize the nation over procedures.

direct-votes.rationale: Populism (working with the people) is a light, but the sources show a party-led, leader-centred movement and no call for referendums; inferred as split.

workers-councils.rationale: The movement was founded in militant anti-communism and statism.

right-to-secede.rationale: The programme says to preserve the unitary national state and rejects ethnic-based status.

natural-rulers.rationale: The leader principle and nation-first elitism suggest a lean towards yes, but no source states natural rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: The Grey Wolves fought leftists on the streets in the 1970s, which undermines a rejection of political violence by a typical adherent.

war-builds-character.rationale: Pan-Turkic idealists spoke of sacrifice for the cause, but no source states this about war.

separate-church-state.rationale: Idealism blends Turkish nationalism with Islamic morals; the programme however endorses a secularism that protects religious freedom.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The party adopted Anatolian Islam but did not adopt radical Islam, and nationalism takes precedence over Islam.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Idealism holds that the state is necessary to protect homeland and nation.

military-superiority.rationale: The programme prioritizes domestic defence capability and the movement stresses a strong state and army.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The movement is described as ethnicist and the Grey Wolves stress an ethno-racial Turkish identity, though Islam is also part of the nation.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The movement is anti-communist; societalism stresses social solidarity within the nation.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Societalism backs equal opportunity and social justice, not equal outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The programme rejects ethnic-based political or legal status for groups.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Anti-imperialist rhetoric appears in MHP discourse, yet no source mentions reparations, and Turkey's own imperial past complicates the claim; left neutral.

civilizational-union.rationale: Pan-Turkic goals of unity with the Turkic world and the Turkish-Islamic ideal favour union among peoples of shared culture.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Societalism holds that activities should benefit society, and the nation comes before the individual.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Idealists were devoted to serving the state and the nation above individual interest.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The programme stresses protecting natural heritage but is not framed as intrinsic value.

limit-population.rationale: A nationalist movement stressing national strength is unlikely to endorse limiting population.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The industrialisation light calls for rapid industrialisation as national development.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Rapid industrialisation and technology are doctrine, but this is bounded by respect for roots and institutions.

human-enhancement.rationale: The scientific-mentality light favours science, but traditional morality would restrain bodily enhancement; no sourced stance, so split.

algorithmic-government.rationale: The leader-and-state-centred doctrine does not envisage algorithmic decision-making.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: A security-minded statist movement would favour state access; inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: Populism joins progress with continuity of roots; adherents seek national renewal, not mere restoration.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Idealists stressed devotion to the ideology and doctrine.

direct-action.rationale: The movement contested elections and joined governments, though street action was common in the 1970s.

means-match-ends.rationale: The sources give no view on prefigurative methods; the movement's street violence and its stated devotion to the state point in different directions.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Industrialisation and technology are central lights.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The doctrine favours industrial development and an organized national society.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Societalism backs social assistance but income remains tied to property and work.

production-for-use.rationale: The programme favours a competitive private-sector economy with exports.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The doctrine rejects Marxism and class conflict, treating property as legitimate.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The movement was founded on stringent anti-communism.

collective-farming.rationale: The programme favours land reform that protects individual farmers and corporatizing farms in producers' favour.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Anti-imperialist discourse exists but the movement is not Marxist.

taxation-theft.rationale: The programme discusses tax fairness and state-run social programmes funded by revenue.

harm-principle.rationale: Morality grounded in national customs and traditions justifies restricting conduct beyond preventing harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The nation and state take priority over the individual in the doctrine, and the programme speaks of national rights.

conscription.rationale: A nationalist movement that prioritizes defence and state strength supports conscription; inferred from its military emphasis.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Idealism is rooted in service to the state and nation; exit-based liberalism is foreign to it.

state-as-business.rationale: State enterprises would be consolidated into one portfolio run for profit, but citizens are not seen as customers; weak lean.

positive-liberty.rationale: Societalism backs social justice, equal opportunity and social security.

media-academia-power.rationale: MHP discourse is populist and critical of elites, but no source claims that universities and media outrank elected officials.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Racial thinking exists in Turkist currents but Idealists made no stated genetic claim about ability.

organic-representation.rationale: Corporatist components existed in the party's tradition but representation by bodies is not stated doctrine.

total-state.rationale: The doctrine stressed a strong state but with mixed economy and individual freedom as a light; not total.

national-rebirth.rationale: Idealism sought to revive Turkish identity, pride and consciousness; the movement is nationalist-revivalist.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Idealists held Great Turan as the final ideal of the party, with influence among Turkic peoples.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The party stresses loyalty to a Basbug leader but not feudal oaths; inferred disagreement.

bound-labor.rationale: The programme calls for land reform in farmers' favour and Peasant care.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Scientific mentality, free of prejudice, is a stated light.

universal-morality.rationale: Morality is tied to the Turkish nation's customs; split.

single-common-good.rationale: Idealists hold that state, homeland and nation form a unity with a single national interest.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Neither the Nine Lights nor the programme sources discuss Zionism; no position can be sourced, so adherents are treated as split.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The programme gives weight to external Turks and Turks abroad; inferred support for return rights of co-ethnics.

revive-national-language.rationale: Turkish is already the state language; the programme insists on Turkish-language instruction.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Societalism stresses harmony and social justice within the nation; worker or public votes over firm governance is not part of the doctrine, so a mild no is inferred.

school-vouchers.rationale: The programme stresses state-guaranteed education and Turkish-language instruction; no voucher proposal.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The programme combines production support with fiscal fairness; no stated line on deficits.

economic-freedom.rationale: Freedom is a light, but the doctrine favours state control of strategic economic activity.

rule-by-example.rationale: Morality emphasises national virtue, but rule by law is not rejected.

national-self-determination.rationale: The movement defends the Turkish nation's independence and Turkic causes abroad, but its programme rejects self-rule for Kurds and other groups inside Turkey, so its view of every nation's right is contested.

force-without-un.rationale: National-interest foreign policy and military emphasis suggest willingness; not stated.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Scientific mentality is a light but Islamic morals and virtues are also integral to Idealism.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Nation-first outlook suggests benefits for citizens; inferred.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Production and work are stressed alongside social protection; not stated.

class-collaboration.rationale: Societalism and the doctrine reject class conflict in favour of national solidarity.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Idealism stresses preserving history, roots and customs.

dominated-front.rationale: The movement uses anti-imperialist discourse, but it was anti-communist and aligned with the West in the Cold War; split.

workers-nation.rationale: Societalism places workers within the nation and rejects international class solidarity.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Morality grounded in traditions suggests this, but the programme opposes legal discrimination against women; weak lean.

ban-interest.rationale: Private-sector dynamism and exports are favoured; Islamic finance is not a stated demand.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The programme calls for opposing legal discrimination and a unitary state of citizens; legal racial segregation is contrary to the Turkish-Islamic nationalist model, which assimilates.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Idealists see the state as the protector of homeland and nation, not an instrument of a class.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The programme seeks oil and gas exploration and energy independence while also stressing clean energy.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The programme insists on Turkish-language instruction and a unitary national state, with no ethnic status for groups.

elite-replacement.rationale: No source attributes a replacement plot to elites; Turkey was a country of emigration in the doctrine's formative years, so the claim has little purchase.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems are not discussed in the sources; the party has competed under thresholds without a stated preference.

national-mission.rationale: Pan-Turkic and Turkish-Islamic ideals involve leading the Turkic world but not spreading a form of government.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The programme opposes discrimination against women but frames this as protection, not a structural patriarchy.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: MHP campaigns used populist and anti-establishment discourse.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from Islamic-influenced morality and a doctrine centred on the family, which sit badly with state discouragement of births.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Idealists identified with the state and security forces they supported.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The doctrine endorses a state controlling strategic activities and providing social security.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Idealism's Islamic dimension and assimilation of peoples in Turkey make this unlikely despite racial currents.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Racial-ethnic Turkish primacy sits against formal equality before the law, which the programme affirms for women; split.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Anti-communist doctrine; the question presupposes a socialism it rejects.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The sources treat Anatolia as the Turkish homeland and never frame states as colonial projects; a mild no is inferred.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The programme asserts a unitary national state and equality before law; secularism protects freedom of conscience.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The programme endorses a secularism protecting freedom of religion and conscience, while Islam is part of national identity; no sourced restriction either way.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The programme calls for state-provided religious education in schools.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The question concerns a socialist state; this anti-communist movement has no position, though its own statism would favour a strong state under threat.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The party competes electorally and claims popular legitimacy; the nation is the source of the state.

trade-surplus.rationale: The programme emphasises exports and high-value production.

population-transfer.rationale: The programme rejects ethnic-status claims; forced transfer is not stated.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The movement saw force as legitimate for protecting the state and the Turkic cause.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Nationalism sees struggle between peoples but societalism stresses solidarity; split.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The party itself was banned after 1980 and sought protection of the unitary state; adherents back banning separatists and communists.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Freedom is a light but not framed as non-domination.

vanguard-party.rationale: Anti-communist; though the movement's own party-leader-doctrine form is vanguard-like.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The programme prioritizes protection of the poor and vulnerable through social programmes.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Public housing sales are not discussed in the sources; the programme's privatization via share offerings gives no clear signal here.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The programme extends union rights but stresses national unity and order.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The doctrine blames underdevelopment and social injustice (industrialisation, peasant care, social justice) rather than population, so a mild disagreement is inferred.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Ethnicist and unitary-state assimilation make this the typical view.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: The leader-centred, state-centred doctrine does not support sortition.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Idealists' anti-communist state-protection mission supported emergency measures.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Social-minded state with control of strategic activities suggests tolerance.

party-controls-media.rationale: The programme calls for a free media without censorship.

party-commands-army.rationale: The programme treats the army as state institution; party command is not part of it.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Nation-first outlook suggests restrictive naturalization; inferred.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: The programme raises pay for village and neighbourhood headmen and does not tie politicians' pay to workers; no sourced support for the idea.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Idealists were organized under strong party discipline and devotion to the ideology.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Mentions EU only as a trade market; Turkey-centred foreign policy and unitary state defend sovereignty.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The sources give no view on the presidential or parliamentary division of command; the party later accepted a presidential system, but the doctrine is silent.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Irrelevant to Islamic context; no position.

clerical-rule.rationale: The party chose the Turkish-Islamic ideal rather than radical Islam, and nationalism overrides Islam.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The movement stressed loyalty to the state and nation in war.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Morality grounded in the nation's customs suggests; the programme however opposes censorship of media.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The sources do not discuss term limits; the party's leader-centred culture would tolerate long tenure, but adherents are not documented as stating this.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall votes are not discussed in the sources; the party's leader principle and party discipline do not settle it.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The party was aligned with the West in the Cold War and not isolationist; the programme speaks of multi-directional policy.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: The programme is a market-friendly, private-sector economic plan with no housing-ownership mandate; banning rentals is far outside it.

people-in-arms.rationale: The programme prioritizes a state army and security forces.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Peasant care, with agricultural towns and village development, is one of the nine lights.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Pan-Turkic goals include union of Turks across borders, with Turkic republics cooperation, and the Great Turan ideal.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Ethnicist Turkish primacy contradicts cultural equality in the movement's discourse.

death-penalty.rationale: The movement has long advocated the death penalty for terrorism; adherents typically agree.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Traditional-morality stance suggests resistance to sex-ed; inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Scientific mentality is a light but religion has a place; split.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Morality grounded in national customs supports restriction.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Ethnic conception of the Turkish nation favours descent.

minority-language-support.rationale: The programme requires instruction at all levels in Turkish and rejects ethnic-based status for groups, so state support for minority languages in schools is opposed.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The programme guarantees freedom of religion and conscience but insists on a unitary national legal order; no sourced view on exemptions.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Conformity with national morality and customs is a core light.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Anti-imperialist rhetoric exists but nothing stated.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Anti-capitalist and anti-imperialist discourse in MHP election appeals; but not systemic transformation.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitution-making procedure is not discussed; the movement defended the existing state order and its unitary-state clause.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Statism and developmentalism suggest tolerance; the doctrine includes freedom as a light so weak lean.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The programme has a nation-first stance yet proposes cooperation with the Turkic republics; global aid duties are not addressed.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The doctrine looks to the nuclear and space era and defence self-reliance.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The programme discusses fairness and productive economy but never addresses central-bank independence.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Nationalist territorial attachment to homeland; irredentist ideals.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Societalism accepts property but opposes its abuse to the nation's detriment.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Anti-communist, but no stated view on the debate.

precautionary-principle.rationale: The programme proposes environmental impact review for hydro projects but also energy-development priorities; no stated precaution doctrine.

collective-defense.rationale: The movement was Cold War aligned with the Western alliance and values collective security; inferred.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Pan-Turkic irredentism and Turkey's own stance on Cyprus cut in different ways; the sources document no position.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The state supplies imams and religious education; Islam under national state; inferred.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The sources do not discuss the head of state's role; the movement's own Basbug figure was a partisan leader.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The programme insists on preserving the unitary national state and ending Kurdish negotiations.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Opposes ethnic-based status and autonomy; unitary state.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The movement is republican; Basbug is a leader title, not divine descent.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The programme speaks of tax fairness and income-tax exemption at the minimum wage, which is progressive-leaning but not a stated position on flat tax.

character-from-environment.rationale: Racial-ethnic Turkist currents stress innate nation, while the doctrine's education and morality emphasis stresses upbringing; split and unsourced.

space-expansion.rationale: The industrial light mentions the space era but not a central goal.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Constitutional theory is not discussed in the sources.

leader-cult.rationale: Turkes was proclaimed Basbug and portraits and cult-like devotion surround leaders.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-law custody presumptions are not discussed; the programme addresses domestic violence and protection of women and children only.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The movement rejects class struggle altogether, so it would reject the premise that it continues under socialism; the question is otherwise outside its concerns.

land-redistribution.rationale: The programme calls for a land reform protecting farmers; the Peasant Care light favours small farmers.

refugee-return.rationale: Return of refugees and descendants is not discussed; no sourced position.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Pan-Turkic ideals concern external Turks and Great Turan.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Secularism that protects religious freedom is stated; nationalism has precedence.

women-must-cover.rationale: The programme opposes legal discrimination against women and does not call for mandated covering.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-Turkic union with the Turkic world is the party's final ideal as documented by Minasyan.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The programme rejects ethnic-based status for groups.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Not discussed; the movement's concern for external Turks could point either to staying and claiming rights or to support from Turkey.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Idealism emphasises ideals, national spirit and morality as driving forces, against materialism.

ban-cartels.rationale: The programme criticises market dominance from privatizations.

no-bailouts.rationale: The programme keeps state enterprises and strategic banks like Ziraat public and favours state protection of the economy, so a mild disagreement with refusing bailouts is inferred.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Judicial constraint of majorities is not discussed; the party backs a strong national state yet also defends constitutional order.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The programme opposes discrimination but no quotas are mentioned.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarky not stated, but domestic production priority.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: The programme addresses domestic labour and environment rules and export promotion but not binding trade-agreement standards.

moral-incentives.rationale: Morality and social duty are lights, but income and property remain.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The Grey Wolves were armed groups, but aimed to protect the state, not make revolution.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The movement is republican and rooted in the Republican Peasants' Nation Party tradition, so hereditary titles are not part of it.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The programme roots nationalism in Turkish history and culture; Turkish-centred education.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Pan-Turkic idealism speaks of kinship with Turkic peoples as brothers, not of tutelage; a mild no is inferred.

patriotic-education.rationale: Nationalism is the first light and the programme calls education in Turkish; devotion to nation and state.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary design is not discussed in the sources.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Cultivating Turkic and Ottoman-region influence; Turkic world is a foreign policy priority.

delink-world-market.rationale: The programme seeks export growth and diversified trade.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Morality and societalism; not part of the doctrine.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The sources do not discuss entrenched rights; the doctrine places freedom among its lights but subordinates individuals to the nation.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial boundary treaties are not discussed; the Turkic-world focus gives no clear stance.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Resistance to rulers is not discussed; the movement stresses loyalty to the state and a strong leader.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The movement operates in a republican parliamentary system and has no monarchist tradition; inferred mild agreement.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics is not discussed in any source.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not discussed; conventional use of animals for food is assumed within the movement's rural and traditional culture.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Societalism sees social duty as important.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Idealists are activist, devoted to the cause.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Anti-imperialist discourse used by MHP; but no theory.

party-own-road.rationale: The question concerns communist parties; the movement is anti-communist, though its stress on national independence would favour each nation choosing its own path.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Priority of domestic production; national self-reliance.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Pan-Turkic irredentism but no specific lost-territory demand.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The programme rejects ethnic-based status for groups, so no sourced support exists, but the question is about settler societies that Turkey is not.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Movement is accused of fascist elements and is anti-communist.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: American history is outside the doctrine; no position can be drawn.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Preserve history and roots; not stated for this question.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: The programme addresses protection of women and children from abuse; male disadvantage is not discussed.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Programme addresses domestic violence against women and children.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Own Turkish-Islamic form and national identity apart from Western models.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Turkes was a coup officer; idealists saw themselves as guardians of the state.

paid-care-work.rationale: The programme gives social protection to the poor and family protection, but does not discuss paying domestic labour.

filial-duty.rationale: Morality and the family tradition within Turkish-Islamic customs.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil-service recruitment is not discussed in the sources.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Strategic assets kept public and domestic production priority.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: A comprehensive state social security system is proposed.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land reform in favour of farmers, individual ownership.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The movement works within a republican parliamentary system and the programme refers to fiscal fairness and accountability; inferred mild agreement.

single-official-language.rationale: The programme's instruction-in-Turkish requirement, together with its unitary national state, makes Turkish the sole common language of schooling and public life.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The programme opposes legal and practical discrimination but frames equality formally; outcome-based discrimination findings are outside it and contrary to nationalist suspicion of group claims.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Morality theme, but industrial growth promoted.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The sources do not discuss covert sponsorship; Turkic-world solidarity could cut either way.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Not discussed; the movement was Cold War-aligned with NATO but no source addresses interventions within a bloc.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local residency restrictions on purchases are not discussed; the programme favours a unitary state but regional development.

job-guarantee.rationale: Employment programmes proposed but no guarantee.

democratic-peace.rationale: Not discussed; the doctrine's foreign policy is nationalist rather than democracy-promoting.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Idealists emphasised loyalty to state and law.

non-intervention.rationale: The sources do not state a general non-intervention rule; the movement backs Turkic and Muslim brethren abroad, which cuts against it.

industrial-unions.rationale: The programme discusses union rights but not craft versus industrial structure.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiratorial rhetoric about external enemies is common but not doctrine.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The morality light and the programme's family protection treat the family as the nation's foundation, so removing legal marriage is rejected.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Open government; programme criticises illegal surveillance.

local-production.rationale: Domestic priority but no stated position.

religious-nation.rationale: Turkish and Muslim identity, but nationalism takes precedence over Islam; ethnic/religious both.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The programme asks for a Turkey-centred, multi-directional foreign policy, not submission to a hegemon; inferred mild disagreement.

defeat-communism.rationale: Strong anti-communism founded the movement's relation to the state.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The programme proposes both state enterprises run for profit and privatization via share offerings but no specific mixed provision of services.

religion-illusion.rationale: Idealism ties Turkish identity to Islamic morals.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The programme opposes legal discrimination against women and protects them from abuse but does not link equality to economic transformation.

socialized-care.rationale: Family protection and traditional customs in the morality light imply housework and childcare stay with families rather than becoming public services.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with internal nations are not discussed; the programme rejects ethnic-based status.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Cooperatives for peasants but not communal society.

majority-settlement.rationale: The programme stresses a unitary state with no ethnic status but does not propose settlement policy.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Fikret Eren described the doctrine as distinct from both socialism and capitalism.

holocaust-denial.rationale: No source discusses the Holocaust; a mild no is inferred since neither the doctrine nor the programme rests on it.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Traditional morality opposes same-sex relations but criminalization is not a documented demand, and homosexuality is not criminalized in Turkey; split.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The movement protected the state against leftists with street force in the 1970s but also contested elections and later criticized state misuse; split.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The programme guarantees freedom of religion and conscience yet Islam is part of national identity; no documented support for punishing blasphemy.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Turkey has no overseas colonies and the doctrine does not discuss them; a mild no is inferred from its anti-imperialist rhetoric.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Idealism treats Islam as a component of Turkish identity rather than a legal programme; no source addresses this doctrine of jihad.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Idealism takes the Turkish-Islamic ideal, not radical Islam, and ranks nationalism over Islamism, so armed removal of rulers for ignoring religious law is rejected.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The leader principle, party discipline and a state-centred doctrine favour representative party politics, though populism (working with the people) tempers this to a mild no.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The movement frames society through nation and state, not through overlapping racism, sexism and class; adherents would reject the framework.

assisted-dying.rationale: Idealism's Islamic morals and respect for traditional customs imply opposition to medically assisted suicide; no source states it directly.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Doctrine claims a third way beyond left and right; inferred.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Islam is part of Turkish identity.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: The programme supports secularism protecting religious freedom; the party was historically sympathetic to the headscarf issue but no sourced position here.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not discussed; the programme opposes abuse against women but says nothing on NDAs or arbitration.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The programme prioritises domestic defence production and Idealists see the army as a pillar of the state, so abolition is firmly rejected.

rich-first.rationale: The doctrine's regional development and peasant-care lights favour balanced growth, while developmentalism accepts uneven growth; no sourced position.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Programme multi-directional but Cold War Western alignment.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The movement is republican and its leader Basbug was a chosen leader, so hereditary succession is contrary to its tradition.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: The programme favours private-sector dynamism and state banks like Ziraat, not user-owned mutual banks.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: MHP discourse includes anti-imperialist criticism but no source documents a position on IMF conditions.

property-franchise.rationale: Societalism and populism ground politics in the whole nation, and the party seeks votes among peasants and low-income groups, so a wealth-based franchise is rejected.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The programme addresses protection of women and the environment separately; no ecofeminist link, so a mild no is inferred.

reification.rationale: This is a Marxist theory of commodity fetishism; the movement's anti-communist, nation-centred doctrine does not use it, and a mild disagreement is inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The programme calls for a free and independent media and an end to political pressure but says nothing on wealth and press ownership.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The programme emphasises rule of law and an independent justice system; inferred mild agreement.

racial-franchise.rationale: The movement is ethnic-nationalist in culture but seeks equal citizenship in a unitary republic and contests elections; limiting the franchise by ethnicity is not part of it.

online-participation.rationale: Digital participation is not discussed in the sources.

open-government-data.rationale: The programme calls for an end to illegal surveillance and for open governance but never addresses publishing decision records.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Traditional Islamic family values favour same-faith marriage, but no documented legal demand exists; split.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Anti-minority boycotts are not part of the doctrine or programme, though some nationalist currents encouraged them; mild no.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Random citizen bodies are not discussed; the movement's leader and party-centred politics would not favour sortition.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Idealism takes Islam as part of Turkish identity but does not propose reinterpretation of doctrine; no sourced stance.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Criticises market dominance and anti-capitalist discourse.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Traditional morality grounded in Turkish-Islamic custom and a martial, state-protective ethos imply opposition, though no source states it.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Idealism links Turkish identity to Islamic morals and virtues and the programme backs state-provided religious education, so state atheism is firmly rejected.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Idealists saw their mission as protecting the state and the programme stresses ending terrorism and anarchy, so abolishing police and prisons is rejected.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Unitary state opposes ethnic power sharing.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits are not discussed; the party's leader culture and the doctrine give no direct guidance.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid delegation is not discussed; the movement's party discipline and leader principle make it an unlikely fit.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not discussed; the doctrine's concerns are national development and security.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Not discussed; Idealism's Turkish-Islamic traditionalism implies reluctance, so a mild no is inferred.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The programme opposes discrimination against women yet the morality light upholds traditional family structures; split.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: A nation-first doctrine and a programme that puts the Turkish nation first imply that political rights belong to citizens, not foreign residents.

rent-control.rationale: Not discussed; the programme favours markets in production but state action in housing is undocumented.

abolish-ip.rationale: The programme emphasises original design, R&D and technology-based competitiveness, which presupposes protection of intellectual property.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Ideal Hearths youth organizations with camps and drills.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: The movement was aligned with NATO, which hosts nuclear weapons in Turkey, while the doctrine looks to the nuclear era; split.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The programme asks for a Turkey-centred foreign policy and domestic defence production, though the party backed NATO membership; split.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Turkish nationalists typically reject recognition of the Armenian genocide, so a mild no is inferred, though the sources do not address it.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Societalism accepts property but opposes its abuse; the doctrine does not say income should reward work over ownership.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The movement glorifies sacrifice and armed defence of nation and state, and the Grey Wolves were armed, so absolute pacifism is rejected.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Traditional morality grounded in national and Islamic custom would reject constructivism about sex.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: The programme speaks of protecting women as a category and opposing their discrimination, the opposite of deconstructing it.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Idealists ready to sacrifice their lives for the cause.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The doctrine's idealism and the willingness to sacrifice life for the cause suggest a moralized politics, but no source states a good-versus-evil frame.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The programme stresses cooperation with external Turks and the Turkic world without saying whether the homeland should gather them or serve as a centre.

culture-before-state.rationale: Idealism cultivates identity and consciousness, yet the movement is state-centred; the order is not documented.

god-not-male.rationale: Not discussed; traditional Islamic theology is assumed so a mild no is inferred.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Not discussed; traditional Islamic culture is assumed so a mild no is inferred.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Ethnicist nationalism with its Turkish-first economy suggests this, but no source states it.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Pan-Turkic aims to unify Turkic peoples across borders imply support for merging their regions, but this is not documented for administrative units.

independent-unions.rationale: The programme extends union rights to more workers but Fikret Eren's doctrinal proposal had mandatory unions outside state control while the movement valued national unity; split.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The movement is anti-socialist and rejects the premise; a mild no is inferred.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The programme keeps strategic assets such as large hydro plants public and runs railways on market principles; mild support inferred for public water and hospitals.

second-chamber.rationale: Bicameralism is not discussed in the sources.

municipal-property.rationale: The doctrine endorses private property within limits and strategic state control, not community ownership of the means of production.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The programme upholds the unitary national state, contrary to confederal municipalism.

family-wage.rationale: The programme proposes raising the minimum wage and family protection; a mild yes is inferred.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Regulatory pace for drugs is not discussed in any source.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not discussed; the programme emphasises R&D funding generally but nothing on ageing.

anonymous-payments.rationale: The programme condemns illegal surveillance but emphasises order and security; untraceable payments are inferred as opposed mildly.

online-anonymity.rationale: The programme condemns illegal surveillance but prioritises state security and order; mild no inferred.

person-over-state.rationale: Idealists identified state and nation as above individual interests and devoted themselves to the state.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Idealism (ülkücülük) is a moral and ideal-driven creed tied to Islamic morals and virtues, implying a spiritual dimension in politics.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The programme preserves the unitary national state, which means regional powers derive from and can be withdrawn by the centre.

gm-crops.rationale: The programme emphasises modernizing agriculture and productivity but also self-reliance in seed supply; no stated position on GM crops.

dense-cities.rationale: The peasant-care light prefers village development into agricultural towns, with no support for urban density.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Scholars describe the Grey Wolves as ethno-racial in their view of Turkishness, but Islam and the state are also central; split.

racial-pride.rationale: Idealism seeks Turkish pride and consciousness in its second light, so pride in ancestry is endorsed.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Idealists held Pan-Turkic union with Turkic peoples as the final ideal and valued military strength, which is incompatible with a strictly defensive doctrine.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Pan-Turkism treats Turkic peoples sharing language and ancestry as one nation across borders and religions.

communal-electorates.rationale: The unitary-state programme with equal citizenship rejects separate electorates by religious community.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The programme calls for preserving the unitary state and ending PKK negotiations, reflecting a Sevres-syndrome tradition of seeing outside powers behind separatism.

free-public-college.rationale: The programme sets education targets and Turkish-language instruction but does not discuss tuition.

pollution-taxes.rationale: The programme proposes environmental impact review but not pollution taxes.

future-generations.rationale: The programme stresses environmental heritage protection and sustainable social security, supporting a mild yes.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The programme opposes discrimination and protects women but does not claim distinctive values to be weighted.

arms-reduction.rationale: The programme prioritises domestic defence production and military capacity, opposing arms reduction.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Diplomatic transparency is not discussed in the sources.

capital-controls.rationale: The programme wants export growth and diversified trade but does not discuss capital flows.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Idealism glorifies the state as protector of nation and homeland, which supports a state arms monopoly in principle despite the party's own armed groups.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Idealists were devoted to serving the state and ready to sacrifice for the nation, so refusing war orders runs against their ethos.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The programme extends union rights in line with modern norms, implying support for collective bargaining.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: The programme exempts minimum-wage earners from income tax rather than topping up incomes; no stated view on credits.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Fiscal rules are not discussed in the sources.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: MHP appeals include anti-imperialist rhetoric yet the programme seeks integration by exports; split.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The movement venerates the existing state and defended it, so smashing it is rejected.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The doctrine proposes a defined third-way mixed economy, not open experimentation.

nature-as-capital.rationale: The programme calls for environmentally sensitive planning but never frames nature as capital.

sacred-nation.rationale: Idealists were ready to sacrifice their lives for the nation, which the doctrine places first of the nine lights.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Student loans are not discussed in the sources.

internal-colonialism.rationale: The programme addresses regional development inequality but rejects ethnic-regional separate claims; a colonial framing is inferred rejected.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Not discussed; Islamic morals suggest a shared nature but nationalist particularism cuts the other way.

public-service-media.rationale: The programme wants free and independent media and an end to political pressure, but does not discuss public broadcasters specifically.

farm-price-support.rationale: The peasant-care light proposes cooperatives that shield peasants from usurers and provide loans and aid.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Idealism joins Turkish identity to Islamic morals and ranks the nation above religion; it never endorses religious pluralism of truth, so this is inferred from its Turkish-Islamic character.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from the movement's hard-line national-security and strong-state stance; it never addressed nuclear arms directly.

workers-own-party.rationale: Inferred from its anti-communism and populist, class-reconciling 'social-mindedness'; it wants one national movement rather than a class party.

ban-fgm.rationale: The practice is not part of Turkish nationalist tradition and the movement stresses modern state authority; inferred, since the sources do not discuss it.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The MHP declaration addresses women's status within a modern legal order and the doctrine does not favour customary male-only inheritance; inferred.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Idealism's Turkic unity aim treats Turkic varieties as branches of one Turkish-Turkic linguistic community; inferred from that Pan-Turkic aim.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: The statist mixed economy favours state direction over private lawsuits as the main remedy; inferred, as pollution law is not discussed.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: It defends a unitary state and elected national parliament and opposes ethnic autonomy, so a formal role for tribal chiefs is inferred to be unwelcome.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: The nation-first, collectivist doctrine subordinates the individual to the national interest, but rapid industrialisation pulls the other way; no stated position.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: The programme stresses security and order; fixed sentences for repeat offenders are inferred from that, not stated.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: The programme insists on Turkish-language education and a unitary national identity, so a language requirement for settlers follows directly.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred from its statist, corporatist outlook that sets national solidarity above class conflict and regulates organised labour.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred from its strong-state, nationalist stress on citizenship and order.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: It joins Turkish identity to Sunni Islamic morals and ranks the nation above religion, so it does not accept equal legal footing for all interpretations; inferred.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Inferred from its priority on the nation and state over procedure; Idealist movements have accepted elections but define legitimacy by national aims.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from its emphasis on family and Islamic morals.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its order-first, strong-state stance.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from its statist mixed economy with social protection rather than market-style replacement of welfare.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred; the declaration speaks of women within family and society and does not contest equal political rights.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred from its Islamic-moral nationalism, which honours religion and the family.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from its Turkish nation-first doctrine, which treats ethnic Turkishness as a real basis of identity.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred as split between traditional family views and acceptance of state institutions.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Idealist writing favours a mixed economy with limited property and never states a first-claim ownership doctrine.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's nation-and-state-first sovereignty, which resists outside courts judging Turkish leaders.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Idealism joins Turkish identity to Islamic morals but subordinates religion to nationalism and states no view on scriptural literalism.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's opposition to ethnic autonomy and its national-unity focus; its conservative family outlook also resists externally pushed gender mandates.

defend-planned-state.rationale: The movement is fiercely anti-communist and anti-Soviet, so defending a planned bureaucratic communist state is contrary to its core.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from the declaration's support for national sovereignty and direct party electoral politics; no council system is stated.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's Turkish-Islamic character and respect for the Directorate of Religious Affairs; no explicit statement on legal status.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The profile summary and Wikipedia article describe the movement as opposed to ethnic autonomy and committed to a unitary Turkish state.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred: it backs Turkic and Turkish self-determination claims such as Cyprus, but dislikes a vote that could split Turkey itself.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Colonial borders are not discussed; its Turkic unity goal implies rejecting Soviet-era borders, while it defends Turkey's own borders.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from its call for rapid industrialisation and modernisation; simple living is not discussed.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred from its unitary Turkish nationalism and hostility to minority-based rights; indigenous settlement is not addressed.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's national-service and militarist tradition, though the declaration does not discuss women's conscription.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: The doctrine centres on a state-homeland-nation trilogy in which the homeland is sacred.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred: it is strongly pro-order and anti-communist, but its programme declares respect for law; killing without trial is not stated.

close-ties-china.rationale: It is fiercely anti-communist and Pan-Turkic in aim, which sets it against alignment with China.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Pan-Turkic aims and care for Turkic and Turkish peoples abroad are central to it.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Inferred: limited private property is part of its doctrine, but common ownership with compensation is not stated.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred: the nation and state take priority, and property is limited by social duty.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Consumption taxes are not addressed in the sources read.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: The declaration offers help for the poor and elderly but no stated choice between targeted and universal.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Inferred: it operates as a party and Idealist Hearths and prizes the state; bypassing organised groups is not stated.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred from its populist, anti-capitalist discourse against favoured big business.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Inferred from its single Turkish-Islamic nation and unitary state, which leave no room for communal religious parties.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: The Nine Lights join science, industrialisation and morality, so modern technology is paired with national and moral values.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred: it accepts the secular civil law of Turkey; divorce is not discussed.

national-resource-control.rationale: Its statist mixed economy and industrialisation light favour national economic control, with an anti-capitalist, populist stance.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Idealism backs limited property and a statist mixed economy but is silent on process versus equality, so inferred and split.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Not addressed in the declarations; no basis for a firm inference.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Not discussed as a theme; Idealists focus on Turkish national unity rather than racial-group advancement.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred from the Nine Lights' placing of the nation and state first, which leaves little room for conscience overriding law.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Anachronistic for the doctrine; its industrialisation drive does not address reduced working time.

multipolar-world.rationale: Inferred from its pan-Turkic aim of Turkic unity as an independent bloc and its distrust of foreign domination.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Inferred from its fierce anti-communism and its rejection of class-based economics.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Inferred from its nationalist solidarism, which treats national loyalty and the welfare of peasants and workers as one.

material-over-identity.rationale: Inferred from its anti-communist, nation-first stance, which subordinates class interest to national identity.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Inferred from its fierce anti-communism and opposition to communist-party rule.

missingStatements.text: When national interest and religious doctrine conflict, national interest should take precedence.
missingStatements.rationale: Idealism was designed to choose nationalism whenever nationalism and Islamism contradict, even though Idealists insist the two are equal.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow tension specific to Turkish-Islamic nationalism; no other ideology in the bank would define itself by it and it would cost every future audit an answer.

missingStatements.text: Farmers should be organised in state-supported cooperatives that protect them from moneylenders and supply credit.
missingStatements.rationale: The peasant-care light proposes cooperatives that shield peasants from usurers and provide loans and aid.

notes: Largely overlaps the Turkish-Islamic synthesis and Turkish nationalism profiles, and may prove indistinguishable from them. Many economic and social-policy answers are inferred from the Nine Lights and the MHP programme, as Turkes's 1975 book was not accessible; the post-Turkes party under Bahceli stresses statism over doctrine.
